panels.rationale: Single frontal facial photo of 6-month-old patient with genetically/clinically diagnosed craniofrontonasal dysplasia per article title and caption. Visible dysmorphic features match caption: broad/bifid nasal tip, facial asymmetry, frizzy/wiry hair. Real patient image, not diagram, no third-party copyright.

At birth, anthropometric measures were as follows: weight 3140 g (81st percentile, +0.89 standard deviations, SD), length 51 cm (95th percentile, +1.65 SD), occipitofrontal circumference (OFC) 33 cm (41st percentile, −0.23 SD), according with the Italian Ines Growth Charts [4]. Physical examination disclosed dysmorphic features, including plagiocephaly and craniofacial asymmetry, prominent frontal drafts, wide and posteriorly rotated ears, epicanthus, hypertelorism, broad and bifid tip of the nose, short and thick philtrum, thin upper lip, high-arched palate (Figure 1).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: Pre-operative patient photo of 5-year-old female in CFND case report; in-text states hypertelorism, visibly widely spaced eyes. B: Pre-operative 3D CT frontal view of same CFND patient showing increased interorbital distance consistent with hypertelorism. C: Pre-operative 3D CT superior view of same CFND patient showing cranial vault suture abnormality consistent with coronal synostosis. D: Pre-operative 3D CT left lateral view of same CFND patient showing cranial suture morphology. E: Pre-operative 3D CT right lateral view of same CFND patient showing cranial suture morphology.

The patient had hypertelorism without ophthalmologic deficits and with normal fundoscopic examination. She had no developmental delay and was performing up to a grade level in school though her parents did endorse some behavioral issues.
